newsitem.title: USA: New York Senate introduces utility tax freeze.
newsitem.headline: New York Senate introduces utility tax freeze.

text.p: Legislation introduced in the New York State Senate would freeze utility taxes for 1997 and begin a phase-out of the state's gross receipts tax on utilities and health care, Majority Leader Joseph L. Bruno said in a statement Tuesday.

The moves are part of the "Jobs for the 21st Century" business tax cut package which would reduce business taxes by $216 million this year and almost $2.5 billion when fully implemented, the statement said.

It said the gross reciepts tax on utilities now provides $710 million a year, while the gross reciepts tax on hospitals, nursing homes, health care clinics and home care providers now provides $550 million annually.
Bruno said the proposal would also provide $60 million of targeted utility tax cuts for economic development.

The Healthcare Association of New York State said it had made repeal of the "sick tax" a high priority this year and noted the Executive Budget had proposed not only to maintain the tax on health care provider income, but to increase the tax rates. The association estimated the governor's proposal would cost providers a total of $352 million in 1997-98.

The utilities operating in New York include Long Island Lighting Co, Brooklyn Union Gas Co, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc, Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, New York State Electric & Gas Corp, Rochester Gas & Electric Corp and National Fuel Gas Co.
